subject: Onboarding benchmark: sprint action sheet & evidence transfer
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Samir Iqbal <samir@ledgerly.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Onboarding benchmark: sprint action sheet & evidence transfer

Samir —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As discussed, we want to run a short benchmark sprint to validate throughput and tail latency for Ledgerly's main inference path before we flip production traffic. Draft plan attached (ledgerly-loadplan-v1.csv). High-level proposed targets:

- Sustained 350 QPS per shard (baseline) with spikes to 700 QPS for 2 minutes
- p95 < 120ms, p99 < 300ms for the full request->response path
- Cold-start / cache-miss tail latency documented separately

What we need from you to start:
1) Confirm a 4-hour pre-prod window on Wed 4/14 (09:00–13:00 PT) when you can route representative traffic
2) A sample traffic dump or synthetic traffic profile (headers, avg tokens per request)
3) Temporary pre-prod API key and a POC contact for run-day ops

Attachments: ledgerly-loadplan-v1.csv (CSV with ramp schedule and request mix)

Next steps: I’ll loop Jordan (on ops) and Monica (CS lead) to own the run. If those targets look off, tell us which numbers to adjust.

Cheers,
Rishi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[rishi@redwood.com]

[Attachment: ledgerly-loadplan-v1.csv (text/csv)]

From: Samir Iqbal <samir@ledgerly.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-13T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding benchmark: sprint action sheet & evidence transfer

Rishi —

Thanks, plan looks good. Couple quick clarifications before we lock the window:

- On tail latency: the p99 target is a little tighter than what we've seen historically for cold cache on our side. Can you confirm whether p99 is measured after warming (i.e., with KV cache primed) or including cold-starts?
- For spikes: we can generate the 700 QPS spike but need to know how long to hold warm-CPU/GPU reservations — is 2 minutes sufficient?

We can provide: a 10k-sample traffic dump (CSV) and a short acceptance matrix (we'll attach separately). Pre-prod key: created a scoped key, will send in a follow-up with the POC (Tasha).

Samir Iqbal
Director, Platform Engineering | Ledgerly
samir@ledgerly.com

[Attachment: ledgerly-acceptance-matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Samir Iqbal <samir@ledgerly.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-14T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding benchmark: sprint action sheet & evidence transfer

Thanks Samir —

To answer: our p99 call should be the measured end-to-end response when running the full suite (so that includes any cache-miss behavior). We'll capture both warm (after a 30min priming run) and cold-start windows and annotate results.

Operational plan for Wed 4/14 (09:00–13:00 PT):
- 09:00–09:30: Environment smoke + priming (warm cache)
- 09:30–10:30: Baseline sustained run at 350 QPS
- 10:30–11:00: Spike testing (700 QPS bursts x 2)
- 11:00–12:00: Long-tail analysis, e2e tracing collection
- 12:00–12:30: Cooldown and log/artifact collection
- 12:30–13:00: Quick readout and action assignment

Run ownership:
- Redwood test harness and runner: Jordan Blake
- Results collection and evidence packaging: Monica Patel
- Customer coordination and throttling controls: Samir / Tasha (Ledgerly)

Test harness: we’ll use k6 with a custom plugin to replay your payloads (we requested the 10k-sample). Please also include header examples and a small set of withheld PII fields that should be redacted. We’ll push artifacts to the Drive folder and post the summary here.

Drive link for artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-Ledgerly-Onboard

Attaching a short ops map (rishi_ledgerly-map.png) that shows where tracing hooks will be placed.

–Monica
Customer Success Lead | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com

[Attachment: rishi_ledgerly-map.png (image/png)]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Samir Iqbal <samir@ledgerly.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding benchmark: sprint action sheet & evidence transfer

Samir —

Appreciate the quick turn on the key. Two quick asks before Wed:
1) Can you drop the sample traffic CSV into the Drive folder (or send it to jordan_blake@redwood.com) by EOD today so Jordan can wire the payload mapping?
2) Please confirm whether Ledgerly will enable payload sampling on pre-prod (we prefer a 1:20 sampling ratio for tracing during the spike runs).

We're standing by to coordinate a 15-min pre-run sync tomorrow morning to walk the runbook and any kill-switch parameters.

Thanks,
Rishi

Date: 2027-04-15T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding benchmark: sprint action sheet & evidence transfer

Rishi / team —

Dropped a condensed traffic profile into the Drive folder (ledgerly-sample-10k.csv). We will enable 1:20 sampling for traces in pre-prod for the run window. Tasha (ops) will be on the call and is listed as the POC.

Also note the traffic pattern includes a 2-minute ramp+peak every 18 minutes to simulate real user behavior — Jordan, you'll see that in the CSV (column: spike_pattern).

Samir

[Attachment: ledgerly-sample-10k.csv (text/csv)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Samir Iqbal <samir@ledgerly.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-16T17:40:00-07:00
Subject: Run summary: preliminary evidence (pre-prod) — next steps

Team / Samir —

We completed the scheduled preliminary run in pre-prod this afternoon. Summary highlights (attached: qps-results-20270415.json):

- Baseline sustained 350 QPS: passed. Observed p50=45ms, p95=110ms, p99=270ms.
- Spike bursts to 700 QPS (2x 2-minute bursts): one burst produced a small tail at p99=420ms (cache-miss window) — we captured traces and a correlated increase in GPU memory pressure on shard-3.
- Cold-start window (first 10 minutes of the smoke test): p99=620ms for cold cache; after priming p99 stabilized below 310ms.

Artifacts uploaded to Drive: qps-results-20270415.json, flamegraphs.tar.gz (profiling shard-3), trace-samples/
Conclusion: baseline targets met. Spike target needs an action to either (a) increase burst capacity on shard-3 for production traffic or (b) tune eviction/priming to reduce cold tail.

Suggested next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive with Ledgerly ops and Redwood inference team (Jordan + infra) — propose Mon 4/19 10:00 PT (30–45m)
2) Action item: Redwood infra (Jordan) to propose a config change to shard burst reservation or provide recommendations for priming TTLs by Tue 4/20
3) Ledgerly to review traces and confirm whether a config change or modest capacity reservation is preferred

Thanks to Samir / Tasha for the traffic and quick responses. We’ll hold a short readout and final acceptance checklist after the deep-dive.

—Jordan
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com

[Attachment: qps-results-20270415.json (application/json)]
